scopeReview: PSO-5.A.1–3: physical/climatic influences including Mediterranean and tropical settings; intensive market gardening, plantations and mixed crop-livestock; extensive shifting cultivation, mobile/nomadic herding and ranching. Inputs per land area differ from farm size or capital per worker.
varietyReview: Seasonal rainfall chart, per-hectare labor table, irregular grazing-zone movement map and staggered fallow-cycle table. Other cases apply all named systems, interactions among soil/water/temperature, human choices and evidence for intensity. Four interpreted stimuli, all five skills and varied keys.
repetitionReview: Distinct mechanisms and denominators: season timing, hours/ha, seasonal resource access and whole-cycle land requirement. All data are original; named practices are applied rather than repeated synonym definitions. No exact stem reuse or numeric-only clone; difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Primary course framework, FAO definitions and original UC climate/rangeland publication checked. All plots, seasons, hours and geometries are synthetic examples. No real farm advice, land-clearing instructions, copied provider material or approved-resource imports. No human review claimed.

questions.correctOption: Account for the dry summer through crop timing, drought-adapted practices or water management rather than assume rainfall is uniform.
questions.independentReview: Checked seasonal totals300+180+20+200=700 and winter/summer ratio15. Seasons are local seasons rather than fixed northern-hemisphere months; the figure supports water-timing analysis, not a precise crop irrigation prescription.
Independently calculated300,10,80 hours/ha and ranked A>C>B. Denominator is cultivated farm area, not workers or output; only labor intensity is measured, so capital intensity is not invented.

questions.correctOption: Using a large changing grazing area can adapt to variable forage and water with relatively low inputs per unit of land.
questions.independentReview: Traced the arrow between supplied seasonal resource points. The example is mobile extensive herding, not a claim that every fixed seasonal route is strictly nomadic rather than transhumant; no permanent residential migration is inferred.

questions.correctOption: 25%; land in fallow remains part of the rotational system rather than disappearing from its land requirement.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed cycle8, cultivated2/8=.25 and fallow6/8=.75. Equal-area plots and evenly staggered phases are explicit; the result would not follow for every unequal or synchronized shifting-cultivation system.

questions.correctOption: Agricultural intensity concerns inputs relative to land, not simply whether a farm is physically small.
questions.independentReview: Checked PSO-5.A.2 explicitly lists plantation agriculture as intensive. No assumption is made that every plantation has identical inputs, working conditions, ownership or crop.

questions.correctOption: Crop and livestock activities can exchange resources within an intensive land-use system.
questions.independentReview: Checked the course’s intensive mixed crop-livestock category and the supplied reciprocal flows. Did not infer zero pollution, complete nutrient closure or whether output is for sale or household consumption.

questions.correctOption: Capital per worker and inputs per hectare are different ratios; wide grazing with low land-relative inputs can remain extensive.
questions.independentReview: Compared capital/worker with input/ha rather than treating them as interchangeable. The scenario supplies low land-relative inputs; no classification is based merely on machinery appearance or ranch size.
Verified the named intensive category in PSO-5.A.2. The classification uses the supplied management pattern rather than assuming every vegetable farm has the same size, income or technology.

questions.correctOption: Warmth affects growing conditions, while soil, rainfall and management still influence which practices are feasible.
questions.independentReview: The leaching condition is explicit for the hypothetical soil, not generalized to every tropical soil. Checked the framework’s physical/environmental influence wording and preserved variation and management agency.

questions.correctOption: Physical geography influences agriculture without uniquely determining every agricultural choice.
questions.independentReview: Compared similar physical conditions with explicitly varying human factors. The answer rejects both environmental determinism and an unsupported claim that climate has no role.

questions.correctOption: Comparable labor, capital and other inputs per unit of land, with the land-use cycle clearly defined.
questions.independentReview: Matched evidence to the classification and retained the possibility of large intensive plantations or small low-input plots. No photo appearance or ownership label substitutes for actual land-relative inputs.
